title: Continuous Subarrays
summary: Given an integer array nums, count the number of subarrays where the absolute difference between any two elements is at most 2.
statement: Given an integer array nums, count the number of subarrays where the absolute difference between any two elements is at most 2. A subarray is defined as a contiguous sequence of elements within the array.
constraints: A subarray is continuous when its maximum and minimum differ by at most two.
Count all nonempty contiguous continuous subarrays.
hints: Maintain increasing and decreasing deques of indices for the window minimum and maximum.
Shrink from the left while their difference exceeds two.
Add right-left+1 valid suffixes for each right endpoint.
After shrinking, every suffix beginning at or after left is valid and every earlier start contains the same invalid extremes.
editorial: After shrinking, every suffix beginning at or after left is valid and every earlier start contains the same invalid extremes.

tests.explanation: The valid subarrays total eight; windows containing both five and two are invalid.
All six nonempty subarrays have range zero.
